answer: Make each agent pay for its identity with scarce work history: an account only gains signing rights by completing verified tasks priced in pigment tokens, with quartz-signed proofs stamped by prior workers, so a fresh ID starts ferrous-poor and worthless. An attacker must actually perform slow, priced labor per identity before earning payouts, meaning mass-registration costs more compute and time than any reward, collapsing the sybil incentive.
